dateline: Hawthorne, CA / Boca Chica, TX — May 2002–Present
heroHeadline: Sept 21-22: Super Heavy B21 Rolls Out for Flight 14, SPCX Closes at $154.72 as Shotwell Files $52M Share Sale
heroSubtitle: 8,906 days since SpaceX founding — Super Heavy booster B21 rolled out to the Pad 2 launch mount at Starbase shortly before midnight Sept 20, reaching the pad about two hours later, as SpaceX continues final preparations for Starship Flight 14 (the program's first full-orbital-insertion attempt), still targeted no earlier than Sept 28. SPCX shares closed Sept 22 at $154.72, up about 1.9% from Sept 21's $151.85 close, as the Nasdaq-100 reweighting's estimated $15.5-22 billion in passive-fund buying continued working through the market. The same day, President and COO Gwynne Shotwell filed to sell 342,170 shares (~$52M) under a pre-arranged Rule 10b5-1 trading plan adopted in June — her first insider sale in three months.
